I will keep my land in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County that is still the most reliable way for me to use the full year, match local heat and water conditions, and protect my income instead of gambling on a more volatile crop. Because I am 65, I want a system that is familiar, mechanized, and manageable, but since I am well educated I will still run it in a more precise way: improved wheat seed, hybrid maize seed, fertilizer at moderate rates instead of chasing yield blindly, and irrigation only at the key growth stages. I am assuming I am planning for 100 mu of land, since no acreage was given. I will plough before wheat to handle residue and level the field, then use rotary tillage before maize for speed. For wheat I will focus on strong stand establishment, one herbicide plus disease and aphid control as needed, and three irrigations at overwintering recovery, jointing, and grain filling if moisture is short. After wheat harvest I will seed summer maize immediately, keep population uniform, apply most nutrients early, irrigate only when the soil actually needs it, and control weeds plus borers and leaf diseases with about two pesticide rounds. I am aiming for steady yields and lower risk, not maximum input.
